title: Origins and History of Auburn Speedster
body:
The Auburn Speedster belongs to the 1928–1936 era and traces to Auburn.

Horse-drawn vehicles ruled for millennia: stagecoaches, Conestogas, hansoms. Benz's Patent-Motorwagen (1886) and Duryea started the auto age; the 1900s saw steam (Stanley), electric (Baker, Detroit Electric — favored by women for clean starting), and gasoline compete. Ford's Model T (1908) and moving assembly line (1913) motorized the masses; the Model A (1927) refined it. The Depression thinned the herd; postwar brought tailfins, V8s, and the interstate. Orphans — Tucker (1948), Kaiser, Studebaker (1966), Packard (1958), Edsel (1960) — are collector legends; the DeLorean (1981) is stainless folklore.

Within that longer story, Auburn Speedster: The 1928; the 1935's. The Speedster is the boattail's icon.

title: How Auburn Speedster Works
body:
Early cars: tiller or wheel steering, planetary (Model T) or sliding-gear transmissions, mechanical brakes (rear only, then four-wheel), hand cranks (then electric starters, 1912 Cadillac). The Model T's planetary transmission used foot pedals for low/high/reverse — driving it is a learned skill. Steam cars (Stanley) flashed water to steam in monotube boilers; early electrics used lead-acid banks and simple controllers. Orphan marques often innovated: Tucker's rear engine and safety features, Studebaker's styling.

title: Historical Road Vehicles Glossary

• brass era — Pre-1916; brass lamps and radiators.

• horseless carriage — The earliest autos; tiller steering.

• orphan marque — Defunct brand (Tucker, Edsel, Studebaker...).

Orphan cars are underdog legends — Tucker fought the Big Three, DeLorean fought physics and the FBI. The hand crank, the bulb horn's 'ahOOga', the backfire on overrun — sensory history.

title: Auburn Speedster Restoration Guide
body:
Mechanical first: brakes, steering, fuel system. Babbitt bearings need specialists. Wood framing: repair, don't bondo. Keep modifications reversible; document everything. Join the marque club before buying.

Restoration order for a Auburn Speedster: 1) document everything photographically before touching it; 2) stabilize (clean, de-corrode, free seized parts); 3) repair before replacing; 4) replace only what is missing or dangerous, marking replacements; 5) test under supervision. Never power an unrestored electrical road vehicle record without a current-limited bring-up.

title: Auburn Speedster — Vintage performance estimator (Runnable Python)
body:
Estimates displacement, gearing, and stopping distance for brass-era and classic cars — the numbers in the showroom brochures.

The program below is real, runnable Python 3. Save it as demo.py and run `python3 demo.py`. It models the core mathematics of the Auburn Speedster so you can experiment with the parameters yourself.
code:
# Vintage auto math: displacement, gearing, braking (public-domain formulas)
import math

def displacement_cid(bore_in, stroke_in, cylinders):
    return math.pi/4 * bore_in**2 * stroke_in * cylinders

# Model T: 3.75 bore x 4 stroke x 4 cyl
print(f"Model T: {displacement_cid(3.75, 4, 4):.0f} CID, 20 hp")
# Flathead V8: 3.1875 x 3.75 x 8
print(f"1932 Ford V8: {displacement_cid(3.1875, 3.75, 8):.0f} CID")

def mph(rpm, tire_dia_in, rear_ratio, top_gear=1.0):
    return rpm * tire_dia_in * math.pi / (rear_ratio * top_gear * 1056)
print(f"Model T at 1600rpm, 30in tires, 3.63:1 -> {mph(1600, 30, 3.63):.0f} mph")

def stop_ft(mph_v, friction=0.4):  # mechanical drum brakes, modest mu
    v = mph_v * 1.46667
    return v**2 / (2 * friction * 32.2)
print(f"stop from 40mph on drums: ~{stop_ft(40):.0f} ft (plan ahead!)")
